Subject: Question on Exhibit F floors/discounts for annual renewal

Rishi —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward the renewal, legal pushed back on a few line items in Exhibit F (pricing schedule). Two asks from their side: one, reduce the 12-month committed minimum by 30% to align with usage variability; two, insert an explicit floor on effective discount (no deeper than 18% off list) so finance can model revenue.

Can Redwood provide language that preserves our ability to offer step-down discounts for higher volume while also keeping a guaranteed minimum $/token floor? If not, can you propose a compromise? We need to close procurement by 10/12.

I'll loop in their contracts contact if helpful.

—Jordan
Contracts, Atlantic AI

Laura / Marissa — forwarding Atlantic's note. Two distinct risks: (1) committed minimum reduction impacts our unit economics for Dedicated capacity; (2) an explicit maximum discount floor may limit our ability to provide promotional pricing in future renewals.

Quick asks:
- Legal language draft from Neha to reconcile a tiered discount schedule with an explicit effective-price floor (can we express floor as $/1000 tokens rather than % to preserve flexibility?)
- Commercial stance: what concessions can we give on minimum commitment (months vs dollars) while preserving safe revenue coverage?

Aditya — can you run a modeled P&L for 70% of the current committed ARR vs current baseline and flag the breakpoints? Need numbers for the next sync with Atlantic (preferably by 10/05).

Thanks —
Rishi

Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Question on Exhibit F floors/discounts for annual renewal

Team —

Attached is a redline of Exhibit F (file: AtlanticAI_ExhibitF_redline_v1.pdf). Summary of proposed language:

1) Commit reduction: allow a one-time, pro-rated reduction of the 12-month committed minimum by up to 25% if Atlantic provides a forecast and a three-month ramp plan; reduction triggers a modest increase to the baseline $/token floor for months 1–3.

2) Discount floor: replace a fixed percent floor with an effective-price floor expressed as $0.0022 per token (annual avg), with an explicit carve-out that volume tier discounts may exceed the floor only if a separate written promotional addendum is signed. This preserves promo flexibility while protecting unit economics.

3) Autoscaling & overage: specify that overage rates apply when actual usage exceeds committed minimums and that overage billing uses the same tiered price table in Exhibit F.

If you approve, I can propose this language to Atlantic. Two areas where we might need exec sign-off: (a) the $/token floor number, and (b) whether we allow promotional discounts without signed addendum.

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: AtlanticAI_ExhibitF_redline_v1.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: RE: Fwd: Question on Exhibit F floors/discounts for annual renewal

All —

Numbers check (high level): Aditya and I ran three scenarios against RBW-2864 forecast:
- Base (no change): ARR preserved, gross margin target 58%
- 25% commit reduction + $0.0022/token floor: ARR down ~22%, gross margin ~54% (acceptable but reduces headroom)
- 30% commit reduction + no floor: ARR down ~29%, gross margin drops below 50% and pushes Dedicated unit economics to unacceptable levels unless we convert to consumption-only billing.

Commercial recommendation: accept Neha's proposal (25% reduction + $/token floor). Offer Atlantic a one-time operational credit (one month of Dedicated capacity) instead of deeper discount. That gives them cash relief without changing long-term unit economics.

If execs sign-off, I'll draft an email to Jordan with a clean Exhibit F and a short explanation of the operational credit.

—Marissa
Director, Commercial Ops

Attachment: RBW_ratecard_summary.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Question on Exhibit F floors/discounts for annual renewal — proposed compromise

Jordan —

Thanks for the patience. After internal review, Redwood can accept a one-time, pro-rated 25% reduction to the 12‑month committed minimum subject to the three-month ramp plan you mentioned. To preserve predictable unit economics we propose the following in Exhibit F (summary):
- Effective-price floor: $0.0022 per token (annualized average);
- Volume tier discounts remain available but any promotional discount that would take effective price below the $0.0022 floor must be documented in a separate signed promotional addendum;
- As a commercial concession, Redwood will apply one month of Dedicated capacity as an operational credit on the first invoice post-amendment (non-recurring).

I've attached a clean copy of Exhibit F reflecting the changes for your review (AtlanticAI_ExhibitF_clean_v2.pdf). If this aligns with Atlantic's needs, please confirm and we will route the amendment for signature. We are targeting execution by 10/12 to meet your procurement window.

Best —
Rishi
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
